title: introduce-policy-dsl-cost-safeguard-runner-and-unit-econ-lint
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation: customer telemetry and recent prefilling/quant autosuggest work showed recurring incidents where tenant-level cost constraints and aggressive quantization profiles resulted in customer-visible quality regressions or unexpected bill spikes. We need a lightweight, auditable, and testable way to declare cost-safeguard policies that translate directly into runtime checks and CI-time linting. This PR introduces a small domain-specific language (Policy DSL) for cost safeguards, a runtime runner that enforces soft/ hard limits at the routing and serving layers, and a CI linter (unit-econ-lint) that validates tenant policy bundles before merge.

What this PR delivers: (1) redwood/costpolicy: a compact Policy DSL (YAML-first, JSON-compatible) and compiler that emits guard rules for the router and the serving runtime; (2) redwood/costpolicy/runner: evaluation library used by the gateway and by Dedicated control plane to block or attenuate requests that would violate tenant policies; (3) CLI: redwood policy apply/dry-run/compile for operators and SEs to validate changes; (4) unit-econ-lint: a CI plugin that validates policy semantics, checks for unreachable rules, and simulates sample workloads to spot risky quantization + batch combos; (5) integration shim in router to perform O(1) policy checks per request and a fallback path that will switch to conservative quant/profiles when a soft threshold is hit.

Design highlights: the DSL centers on three primitives: thresholds (absolute and relative cost/unit), signals (latency, token-rate, quality-regress indicators), and actions (attenuate-batch-size, prefer-legacy-model, refuse-model, downgrade-quant-profile). Policies are scoped at organization, tenant, and route levels. The compiler produces a compact decision graph that the runner evaluates with minimal allocations. The decision graph supports short-circuiting, stochastic rate-limiting, and graceful fallbacks (e.g. prefer-legacy-model + cached-response on overload).

Migration & rollout plan: default_policy.yaml is introduced as an admin-managed tenant fallback. No tenant changes by default. We roll the runner behind a feature flag, first in staging (2 days soak with traffic mirroring), then Canary in us-west with 5% traffic, then progressive ramp on Dedicated tenants who opt-in. The CLI supports dry-run modes for admins to preview simulated unit economics changes.

Testing and benchmarks: added unit tests (compiler semantics, edge-case precedence), integration tests (router + runner end-to-end), and a microbenchmark showing ~0.9us median overhead per request for the O(1) check in the router when the decision graph is cached. Load test scenarios included a stress profile where aggressive quant + large batch would previously exceed predicted unit cost; the runner prevented a spike by switching to conservative quant profile automatically.

Checklist:
- [x] DSL spec and examples (docs included)
- [x] Compiler and decision-graph output format stable
- [x] Runtime runner integrated with router and dedicated control plane
- [x] CLI commands with dry-run and compile subcommands
- [x] unit-econ-lint CI check added to policy directories
- [x] Migration guide and rollout playbook included
- [x] Performance microbench and integration load test results attached

Related work and references: builds on prior prefilling and quant profile work (see ENG-2154, pr-34177, pr-524681) but focuses on operational guardrails rather than autosuggest. Also complements cost-snapshotter telemetry changes in pr-104202.

Release notes: operational feature - add Policy DSL and runtime policy runner; admins can define tenant cost-safeguards (default off). Backwards-compatible by default but recommended for high-spend tenants.

High-level commits summary: 1) add DSL spec + examples; 2) implement compiler and serializer; 3) implement runner and router hook; 4) add CLI and dry-run; 5) unit-econ-lint CI integration; 6) docs + migration guide + tests.

Files of interest changed: see files_changed list below.

How to exercise locally: see docs/costpolicy/README.md - compile sample policy and run redwood policy dry-run --sample-traffic=small; to simulate failover use policy action refuse-model/downgrade-quant-profile.

Security considerations: policies are validated server-side and only admin-scoped policies can perform hard refusals. The runner enforces policy decisions within the serving process; no new network paths introduced. Audit logs added for every policy-triggered action for compliance and postmortem.

Rollout notes for SRE and Support: we added a feature flag redwood.policy_runner.enabled and a per-tenant opt-in toggle. SRE playbook included in docs/playbooks/policy-runner-incident-playbook.md.

Migration note for SDKs: no immediate SDK changes; we will expose a policy validation endpoint in the API in a follow-up small PR.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor — The DSL looks concise. Two asks: (1) show an explicit example where multiple rules with overlapping scopes resolve predictably; (2) can we make the decision graph serialization backward compatible?
Maya Chen — Responding: added deterministic precedence rules and an example in spec.md; compiler emits a version field in the graph for compatibility and we validate on load.
Priya Nair — Suggest adding a safety net if the runner fails (fail-open vs fail-closed debate). We should default to fail-open for low-risk actions and fail-closed for hard refusals.
Maya Chen — Updated runner: soft actions are fail-open by default; hard actions are fail-closed and require admin credential to deploy. Note added to playbook.
Diego Alvarez — CI lint looks heavy; can we run unit-econ-lint with sampling in PRs and full simulation in nightly?
Maya Chen — Implemented sampled mode in CI; full simulation runs in nightly integration job (ci/policy-lint.yml updated).
